cards.text: Jacob has been working for his father-in-law Laban, and Jacob has gotten rich. Now word gets back to Jacob about what Laban's sons are saying about him. And friend, it is NOT a thank-you card.

cards.question: What are Laban's sons saying about Jacob?

answers.text: He built all his wealth off their father
He spends too little time with the flocks
He still owes their father a year of work

cards.question: Jacob can see on Laban's face that Laban's attitude toward him has changed.

cards.text: Gossip from the brothers-in-law. A whole new look on the father-in-law's face. And right in the middle of all that, the LORD speaks to Jacob.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Jacob to do?

answers.text: Go back to the land of his fathers
Stay and make peace with Laban's sons
Take all his flocks down into Egypt

cards.question: Along with that command, the LORD promises Jacob that He will be with him.

cards.text: So Jacob sends for Rachel and Leah, Laban's daughters and his own wives, and calls them out to the field where his flocks are. A family meeting in a field full of sheep. Friend, that is a LOT of listeners.

cards.question: Jacob tells his wives their father's attitude toward him has changed. But what does Jacob say has been with him?

cards.text: Jacob says he served their father with all his strength. Meanwhile Laban kept cheating him by changing his wages, which is like your boss rewriting your paycheck every time you turn around.

cards.question: Jacob says Laban changed his wages ___ times.
Jacob says that with all that cheating, Laban was able to harm him.

cards.text: Jacob tells them that if Laban said the speckled ones would be his pay, the whole flock had speckled babies. And if Laban said streaked, the whole flock went streaked, like the animals were READING THE CONTRACT.

cards.question: So Jacob tells his wives that ___ has taken away their father's livestock and given them to him.

cards.text: Then Jacob tells them about a dream he had while the flocks were breeding. In the dream, the angel of God called out, "Jacob!" and Jacob answered, "Here I am."

cards.question: In Jacob's dream, the angel tells him to look up at the males mating with the flock. What are they like?
Why does the angel in Jacob's dream say this is happening?

answers.text: He has seen what Laban did to Jacob
Jacob asked Him for a bigger flock
Laban's sons needed to be humbled

cards.text: Then the angel says, "I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the pillar and made a solemn vow to Me."

cards.question: In the dream, Jacob is told to wait for Laban's blessing before he leaves.

cards.text: Jacob has told Rachel and Leah everything, dream and all. Now his wives answer, and they start with a question: do they have any share left in their father's house?

cards.question: Rachel and Leah say their father treats them like outsiders.
What else do Rachel and Leah say their father did?

answers.text: Sold them and wasted the money

cards.question: Rachel and Leah say the wealth God took from their father belongs to them and their children.
Rachel and Leah's answer to Jacob: do whatever ___ has told you.

cards.text: Then Jacob gets up, puts his children and wives on camels, and drives all his livestock and everything he gained in Paddan-aram out ahead of him. Friend, that's not packing up, that's a PARADE.

cards.question: Where is Jacob headed with his whole household?

answers.text: To his father Isaac in Canaan
To his brother Esau in Seir
To the far country of Moab

cards.text: Now, all this is happening while Laban is out shearing his sheep. And while he's gone, somebody in Jacob's family takes something of his.

cards.question: While Laban is out shearing, ___ steals Laban's household idols.
Before he goes, Jacob tells Laban he's leaving.
Jacob flees with everything he has. What river does he cross?

cards.text: Across the Euphrates he goes, headed for the hill country of Gilead. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story is FAR from finished.

findings.problem: Two of this card's three beats retell what cards 1 to 3 already covered: the sons' talk (31:1) and Laban's changed face (31:2). Only the last beat, the LORD speaking (31:3), moves the passage forward. The card is mostly a recap, which is also why its citation is stretched to 31:1-3.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: The card is only a bare quote of 31:13, with no storyteller line and none of Papa Dorin's voice. This is the moment the dream's speaker identifies Himself as the God of Bethel, and the card just reads the verse.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card says "all this is happening while Laban is out shearing his sheep," which ties Jacob's whole departure to the shearing. Genesis 31:19 ties the shearing only to Rachel stealing the household idols. It does not say when Jacob's departure happened in relation to the shearing.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
